tool.name: ShapeMetricsWidthTable
tool.summary: Pick a polygon or line layer, name an Output Table and press Run; the optional outputs draw the inscribed circles and give a copy of your layer with the measures. Writes one row per polygon or line feature with its shape measures, on a Basic licence. For polygons the measure that Esri's tools do not give is the maximum inscribed circle (the largest circle that fits inside; radius, centre, and optionally the circles drawn as polygons). Alongside it the table has area, perimeter, Polsby-Popper, Schwartzberg, Reock, solidity, the minimum-area oriented rectangle and the minimum width of the convex hull, several of which Esri tools also give (see Usage). For lines: length, straight-line chord, sinuosity and the oriented rectangle. The tool does not measure the narrowest local width of a polygon. Optional outputs: a copy of the input features with the measures joined, the inscribed circles (centres and circles), the oriented rectangles and an Excel or CSV report.

param.name: out_table
param.dialogReference: Output table, one row per input feature (key SRC_OID).

param.name: precision_m
param.dialogReference: Tolerance in metres of the maximum inscribed circle radius (polygons). Smaller is slower. Must be a finite number greater than zero and at most 10,000 km (10,000,000 m); a Precision above a part's larger bounding-box side is used as that side. A floor of 0.01 % of the feature's larger bounding-box side applies; the reported INSC_TOL is never more than HULL_MINW / 2 - INSC_R.

param.name: copy_attributes
param.dialogReference: Also copy the input attributes to the output table.

param.name: out_centres
param.dialogReference: Optional point feature class: centre of each polygon's maximum inscribed circle with its radius.

param.name: out_circles
param.dialogReference: Optional polygon feature class: the maximum inscribed circle of each polygon drawn as a polygon, with its radius (polygons only).

param.name: out_rectangles
param.dialogReference: Optional polygon feature class: the minimum-area oriented bounding rectangle of each feature.

param.name: out_features
param.dialogReference: Optional feature class: a copy of the input features (geometry as stored, all copyable attributes) with the measures of the table as extra fields, ready to symbolise.

param.name: out_report
param.dialogReference: Optional Excel (.xlsx) or CSV report with Summary and Detail sheets.

param.name: feature_count
param.dialogReference: Number of rows written to the table (derived).

tool.usage:
How to use: choose a polygon or line layer, set Output Table and press Run. To see the result on the map, also set Output Features With Metrics (a copy of the input whose attribute table carries the measures; symbolise it by INSC_R, POLSBY_PP or ASPECT) and, for polygons, Output Inscribed Circles (the largest circle that fits in each polygon, drawn as a polygon). Without Output Features With Metrics, join the table yourself: Add Join with the layer's ObjectID field as Input Join Field, the Output Table as Join Table and SRC_OID as Output Join Field (Add Relate with the same two fields keeps the tables separate). SRC_OID is the ObjectID of the input feature.

What this tool adds, and what Esri already does. The one measure that the Esri tools checked for this help do not give is the maximum inscribed circle (INSC_R, INSC_X, INSC_Y: the largest circle inside the polygon, holes respected). The other fields are in the table so that one run gives them together, but Esri tools already give the same quantities: area and perimeter (Calculate Geometry Attributes), Polsby-Popper and Schwartzberg (one Calculate Field line from area and perimeter, for example 4 * pi * area / perimeter ^ 2), and the minimum-area rectangle (MRR_LONG, MRR_SHORT, ORIENT_DEG) and the minimum width of the convex hull (HULL_MINW), which equal Minimum Bounding Geometry with Rectangle by area and Rectangle by width. If you only need those, use Minimum Bounding Geometry. Beyond that, this tool gives solidity, Reock (area / smallest circle around the feature itself), the internal consistency check and, for lines, chord and sinuosity in the same table.

What 'width' means here. The tool does not measure the narrowest part of a polygon (the local minimum width; that needs a medial axis or a buffer test and is not provided). It gives three different numbers. HULL_MINW is the minimum width of the convex hull, the narrowest parallel-sided strip that holds the whole feature (the minimum Feret diameter); for a concave polygon it is the width of the hull, not of the narrowest part. INSC_R is the radius of the maximum inscribed circle, so 2 x INSC_R is the WIDEST place of the polygon: a fat polygon with a thin neck has a large INSC_R, so do not use it to accept or reject narrow features. 2 x INSC_R is always at most HULL_MINW. STRIP_W (2 x area / perimeter) estimates the width of elongated shapes and is only a rough guide for fat ones.

INSC_R is exact for the centre found (INSC_X, INSC_Y) and at most INSC_TOL below the true maximum. INSC_TOL is the Precision you give, but never less than 0.01 % of the feature's larger bounding-box side (a precision floor, so long strips stay fast), and never more than HULL_MINW / 2 - INSC_R: no circle inside a polygon can have a radius above half the hull width, so a rectangle, however long, gets INSC_TOL 0. For a long thin polygon that is curved or winding the floor can still be larger than the radius itself (a thin arc of 50 km radius and 3 m width has a floor of 5 m for a radius of 1.5 m): such rows are flagged INSC_COARSE (INSC_TOL above 10 % of INSC_R or above 4 times the Precision you gave). The search is limited to a number of cells per part (about 149,000 for polygons with few edges, falling to 20,000 at 5,200 edges or more); a long, thin, winding polygon (river, canal, 5,000 to 15,000 vertices) can use them all and take several seconds on its own (in a sandbox up to about 17 s for 8,800 edges; the budget is sized by a work model of about 3 s, not a time limit), and below 20,000 vertices it is not announced. It is then flagged INSC_CAPPED and INSC_TOL is the upper bound of the error derived from the cells not yet explored (for a multipart polygon it also covers parts searched but not chosen).

Run time in ArcGIS Pro 3.3.2, rounded out with a margin of a few seconds so that it covers every Pro run of this tool so far (the measured times of the Pro runs are in the tool page docs/tools/ShapeMetricsWidthTable.md): 3,000 building footprints with table, centres, rectangles and report about 12 to 19 s (about 3 to 5 s of it measuring); with Output Inscribed Circles and Output Features With Metrics added about 15 to 26 s (about 3 to 6 s measuring); 2,000 road lines about 4 to 7 s; 488 real land-use polygons (median 5 vertices, largest 147) about 15 to 22 s for the whole run (about 1 to 2 s measuring); one built regular polygon of 20,501 vertices about 4 to 5 s for the whole run (under 0.3 s measuring). Footprint-sized polygons are cheap; long, thin or very large polygons are not. Measured in the Python core of the tool in a Linux sandbox (precision 0.05 m): about 1 s for a 2 m wide strip of 2 to 200 km, so a layer of thousands of such strips takes about an hour; a winding band 12 m wide took 4.9 s with 5,000 vertices, 12.7 s with 20,000, 22.6 s with 60,000 and 35 s with 150,000; a coastline-like polygon 7.2 s with 19,000 vertices and 30 s with 150,000. A feature with 20,000 or more vertices is announced before the measuring starts, and the run reports the total time and the slowest feature. To speed up a layer of very long or very large polygons, run a selection first or raise the Precision.

Measures are taken in the plane of the input coordinate system and converted to metres with its linear unit; they are not corrected for map-projection scale. Geographic systems, a missing coordinate system, Mercator systems (Web, World, PDC and regional; not Transverse Mercator such as UTM), the other cylindrical world systems (Plate Carree, Equidistant Cylindrical, Miller, Cylindrical Equal Area), other world-scale systems (Mollweide, Robinson ...) and polar stereographic systems are refused with the fix (Project to a local projected system first). These systems are recognised by name and WKID; a custom system with an unusual name is not. INSC_X and INSC_Y are in the input units.

Multipart polygons: area and perimeter are totals, the hull, rectangle, circle and Reock/solidity use the whole feature (flag MULTIPART), and the inscribed circle is the largest over the parts (INSC_PART). Run Multipart To Singlepart first for per-part measures. For multipart lines chord and sinuosity are empty.

FLAGS lists notes: DEGENERATE (the net area is zero or there is no length; a figure-eight whose lobes cancel is also reported so), MULTIPART, ORIENT_TIE (the minimum-area rectangle is not unique, for example squares, circles, and acute and right triangles; an obtuse triangle has one: MRR_LONG, MRR_SHORT, ASPECT, ELONGATION and ORIENT_DEG are then one of several equally small rectangles; area, RECT_FILL and HULL_MINW do not depend on the choice), INSC_CAPPED, INSC_COARSE, EDGE_X (two edges cross: invalid geometry, run Check Geometry / Repair Geometry), EDGE_X_SKIPPED (more than 20,000 edges, crossing not tested), CLOSED (line whose ends meet), BAD_COORDS (a coordinate is NaN or infinite: the row has no measures and the run warns), NULL_GEOM, DENSIFIED (true curves were densified, so the values are approximate), FAILED, WRONG_WINDING (an outer ring lies inside another outer ring of the feature: almost always a hole stored with the winding of an outer ring, counted as a part, so PARTS, HOLES, AREA_M2 and INSC_R are wrong; run Check Geometry / Repair Geometry), ZERO_RING (a ring without area, such as an out-and-back spike, was left out of every measure; Repair Geometry removes it). Every input feature gets a row. When the Precision you gave makes the INSC_R of a feature rough (INSC_COARSE, or INSC_TOL above 10 % of INSC_R, with the tolerance set by the Precision and not by the 0.01 % floor or the cell budget) the run warns and advises a Precision of at most 5 % of their smallest INSC_R; this also covers concave shapes, whose HULL_MINW / 2 is far above the radius (if the search found INSC_R 0 for one of them, the advice is 5 % of HULL_MINW / 2 and says so). No warning is given when the hull bound made INSC_R exact.

ORIENT_DEG is the azimuth of the long side of the rectangle in degrees clockwise from grid north (the north of the plane of the projection, not true north; in UTM they differ by up to about 3 degrees), 0 to 180 (a line has no direction). Polygons are measured as stored and not repaired.

Output Inscribed Circles: each circle is drawn as a polygon with 72 vertices on the circle, so it lies inside the true circle and therefore inside the feature (its area is 0.13 % below pi x radius squared); RADIUS_M is the exact radius. Output Features With Metrics: the input geometry is copied as it is stored (Z and M values are not kept) with the measures and the input attributes; the ObjectID of the copy is new, SRC_OID is the ObjectID of the input.

A shapefile or dBASE output cannot store an empty number: empty numbers are stored as 0 and the run warns about it. Use a geodatabase output to keep them empty.

A copied field keeps its field-level domain when the output geodatabase has it (a warning names the fields that lose it); subtypes are not carried. Selections and definition queries on the input layer are honoured. The input is never edited.

Other Esri tools: Calculate Polygon Main Angle needs a Standard or Advanced licence (Esri tool page, read 2026-11-08) and is meant for orthogonal polygons. Zonal Geometry (THICKNESS) needs the Spatial Analyst extension at every licence level; its zones can come from an integer raster or a feature layer and the result is a raster of the deepest point of each zone, not a vector circle with a centre and a radius (Esri page https://doc.esri.com/en/arcgis-pro/latest/tool-reference/spatial-analyst/zonal-geometry.html, read on 2026-11-07). Outside ArcGIS Pro the maximum inscribed circle is also in shapely 2.1 (maximum_inscribed_circle) and PostGIS 3.1 (ST_MaximumInscribedCircle), and QGIS Pole of inaccessibility stores the same radius (distance from the pole to the boundary) in the field dist_pole.

Not verified: a Basic licence (the tool calls nothing above Basic, but Basic compatibility is not verified); in ArcGIS Pro the shapefile, selection and overwrite cases of the smoke test and the WRONG_WINDING, ZERO_RING and BAD_COORDS paths (simulated arcpy only; in ArcGIS Pro arcpy did not store a NaN coordinate, and such a feature arrived without geometry and got NULL_GEOM). Multipart polygons and polygons with 20,000 or more vertices were exercised in ArcGIS Pro on built features only, not on real data. The numbers are also checked against shapely in the development tests.
